significance: A Paadal Petra Sthalam in Viluppuram district whose original Chola complex was rebuilt in masonry by Vijayanagara kings in the 16th century. It was converted into a stone temple under Parantaka I around 940 CE and carries inscriptions of the medieval Cholas, the Pandyas and the Rashtrakutas.
story: Local legend explains the older name Thirumundeeswaram from the gatekeepers Thindi and Mundi who worshipped Shiva here; another account has King Chokkalingam find a lingam beneath a lotus while hunting and raise the temple over it.
